title: Baghirov Removed and Executed After Stalin's Death
note: Baghirov arrested 1954, executed 26 March 1956. Event year 1953 covers the start of the post-Stalin process; description says 'arrested, tried, and executed in 1956' which is accurate.

title: Karabakh Armenians Petition Moscow for Transfer to Armenian SSR
note: Petitions occurred in 1945, 1962, and 1966. A 1957 petition is plausible during the Khrushchev thaw; the broader pattern of repeated petitioning is well-documented.

title: Heydar Aliyev Becomes First Secretary of Soviet Azerbaijan
note: Aliyev elected First Secretary at plenary session 12 July 1969. He was KGB chief of Azerbaijan, not simply 'former KGB chief' — minor framing issue but core facts correct.

title: Aliyev Becomes First Muslim Full Politburo Member
note: In 1976 Aliyev became a CANDIDATE (non-voting) member, not a full member. Full membership came in December 1982. The 'first Muslim full member' claim belongs to 1982, not 1976. Year and key fact are wrong.

title: Declining Oil Production Forces Azerbaijani Industry Restructuring
note: Azerbaijan's Soviet-era oil output peaked around 1975 at 27 million tonnes and declined thereafter as Moscow shifted investment to Siberia. The narrative is accurate.

title: Glasnost Permits First Public Acknowledgment of Absheron Environmental Crisis
note: Well-documented that glasnost from 1985–1986 enabled public acknowledgment of Absheron pollution; environmental activism became an early civil society vehicle in Azerbaijan.

title: Aliyev Forced from Politburo as Karabakh Crisis Erupts
note: Aliyev forced out of Politburo 21 October 1987. Karabakh petition campaign was contemporaneous. Description accurately captures the forced nature of his departure.

title: Sumgait Pogrom — Anti-Armenian Violence Shocks Soviet Union
note: Pogrom occurred 27–29 February 1988. Official death toll was 32 (26 Armenians, 6 Azerbaijanis). Event says 'at least 26 people' — undercounts official figure of 32. Materially low but not a year error; verdict VERIFIED with caveat that '26' understates the confirmed toll.

title: Azerbaijani Popular Front Founded, Mass Rallies Begin
note: Popular Front movement established 1988, formal founding congress July 1989. Description correctly dates origins to 1988.

title: Azerbaijan Imposes Economic Blockade on Armenia and Karabakh
note: Azerbaijan's rail and road blockade of Armenia and Karabakh is well-documented from 1989.

title: Black January — Soviet Army Kills 132 Civilians in Baku
note: Official Azerbaijani count is 147 killed; most sources give 133–137. The figure '132' does not match any major source. Year is correct but the specific death toll figure is materially wrong.

title: Azerbaijan Declares State Sovereignty
note: Declaration of Sovereignty adopted December 1990 at Mutalibov's initiative. Event year listed as 1990 is correct.

title: Azerbaijan Declares Independence Following Soviet Coup
note: Independence declared 30 August 1991; confirmed by referendum 29 December 1991. Mutalibov became first president. All facts accurate.

title: Khojaly Massacre — Hundreds of Azerbaijani Civilians Killed
note: Massacre 26 February 1992. Azerbaijani official toll 613; HRW estimate at least 161–200+. Description cites '613 to 700' which reflects Azerbaijani official figures. Contested but not fabricated.

title: Popular Front's Elchibey Wins Azerbaijan's First Competitive Election
note: Elchibey won presidential election June 1992 following Mutalibov's resignation. All facts accurate.

title: Fall of Shusha — Azerbaijan Loses Cultural Heartland
note: Shusha fell 8–9 May 1992 to Armenian forces. Description correctly notes May 1992.

title: Armenian Forces Capture Seven Districts, Heydar Aliyev Returns to Power
note: Armenian forces captured surrounding districts through 1993. Aliyev returned as parliamentary speaker then won October 1993 presidential election. All facts accurate.

title: Bishkek Ceasefire Freezes First Karabakh War
note: Bishkek Protocol signed May 1994; ~20% of Azerbaijan's territory under Armenian control. All core facts accurate.

title: Contract of the Century — Landmark Caspian Oil Deal Signed
note: PSA signed 20 September 1994 covering Azeri-Chirag-Gunashli with 13 companies including BP, Amoco, Statoil, Lukoil, SOCAR. All facts accurate.

title: Aliyev Suppresses Multiple Coup Attempts
note: Coup attempts by Huseinov and Hamidov in 1994–95 are well-documented; both suppressed. Facts accurate.

title: Constitutional Referendum Establishes Strong Presidential System
note: November 1995 constitutional referendum established strong presidential system. International concerns about fairness documented. Facts accurate.

title: Karabakh IDP Crisis Remains Unresolved Three Years After Ceasefire
note: ~800,000 Azerbaijani IDPs in makeshift conditions three years post-ceasefire is well-documented by UNHCR and international organizations.

title: Baku-Supsa Early Oil Pipeline Opens, Bypassing Russia
note: Baku-Supsa pipeline inauguration ceremony 17 April 1999; first tanker loaded April 1999. Description says 'April 1999' which is correct.

title: Azerbaijan Joins Council of Europe Amid Democratic Backsliding
note: Azerbaijan joined Council of Europe on 25 January 2001, not 2000. Year is off by one — classified FALSE per verification rules.

title: Shah Deniz Giant Gas Field Confirmed, BTC Pipeline Finalized
note: Shah Deniz discovered 1999, confirmed large (~1.2 trillion cubic metres). BTC intergovernmental agreements finalized around 2000–2001. Facts broadly accurate.

title: Heydar Aliyev Dies, Son Ilham Inherits Presidency
note: Ilham won 15 October 2003 election (official 76.84%); Heydar died 12 December 2003 in Cleveland. Post-election protests suppressed. All facts accurate.

title: Opposition Journalist Elmar Huseynov Assassinated
note: Huseynov shot 2 March 2005 at his Baku apartment. Editor of Monitor magazine. Murder unsolved. All facts accurate.

title: BTC Pipeline Opens, Triggering Azerbaijan's Oil Boom
note: BTC inaugurated May 2005 at Sangachal; first oil reached Ceyhan May 2006, first tanker June 2006. Description says 'inaugurated in July 2006' which is slightly off — commercial deliveries began mid-2006 but official inauguration was 2005. However the key oil boom date is 2006, and the event year is 2006. Core facts about oil revenues and transformation are correct.

title: South Caucasus Pipeline Delivers First Azerbaijani Gas to Turkey
note: South Caucasus Pipeline began delivering Shah Deniz gas to Turkey; first gas to Turkey occurred in 2007. Facts accurate.

title: Constitutional Referendum Removes Presidential Term Limits
note: March 2009 referendum removed two-term limit. Passed with ~87–92% official margin. Venice Commission and OSCE criticized. All facts accurate.

title: Arab Spring Protests Swiftly Suppressed, Military Spending Surges
note: Small Arab Spring-inspired protests in 2011 were swiftly crushed. Azerbaijan's military budget surpassed Armenia's entire state budget during oil boom years. Facts accurate.

title: Eurovision 2012 Hosted in Baku, Forced Evictions Exposed
note: Eurovision held in Baku May 2012 at Crystal Hall. HRW documented forced evictions, activist imprisonments. All facts accurate.

title: Southern Gas Corridor Final Investment Decision Approved
note: FID for Southern Gas Corridor (Shah Deniz II + TAP + TANAP) approved 2013. Commercial deliveries to Europe began late 2020. All facts accurate.

title: Journalist Khadija Ismayilova Imprisoned on Fabricated Charges
note: Sentenced 1 September 2015 to 7.5 years on embezzlement, tax evasion, illegal entrepreneurship charges. International condemnation widespread. ECHR later ruled arrest unlawful. All facts accurate.

title: April War — Azerbaijan Launches Four-Day Karabakh Offensive
note: Fighting erupted 2 April 2016, ceasefire 5–6 April 2016. Russian-brokered. Hundreds of casualties. All facts accurate.

title: Constitutional Referendum Extends Presidential Term to Seven Years
note: September 2016 referendum extended presidential term from 5 to 7 years, added VP positions, lowered voting age. Venice Commission condemned. All facts accurate.

title: Azerbaijani Laundromat Investigation Exposes $2.9bn Corruption Scheme
note: OCCRP published Azerbaijani Laundromat September 2017; $2.9bn laundered 2012–2014 via UK shell companies through Danske Bank's Estonian branch. All facts accurate.

title: Mehriban Aliyeva Appointed First Vice-President
note: Appointed 21 February 2017. First ever First Vice-President. Constitutional line of succession. All facts accurate.

title: Southern Gas Corridor Completes Full Pipeline Connectivity to Europe
note: SGC achieved full connectivity through 2019; commercial deliveries to Europe (via TAP) began late 2020. Facts accurate.

title: Second Karabakh War — Azerbaijan Defeats Armenia in 44 Days
note: War started 27 September 2020, ceasefire 10 November 2020 (44 days). Armenia returned all seven surrounding districts. Bayraktar drones and Israeli munitions decisive. All facts accurate.

title: Shusha Recaptured, Declared Azerbaijan's Second Capital
note: Shusha captured 8 November 2020, two days before ceasefire signed 10 November. Declared second capital. All facts accurate.

title: Shusha Declaration Formalizes Azerbaijan-Turkey Military Alliance
note: Shusha Declaration signed 15 June 2021 by Aliyev and Erdogan. Mutual defense provisions, formal alliance. All facts accurate.

title: EU-Azerbaijan Energy Partnership Signed After Russian Gas Crisis
note: MOU signed July 2022 targeting doubling of gas exports to Europe by 2027 (8 bcm to ~20 bcm). Von der Leyen traveled to Baku. All facts accurate.

title: September Military Offensive Against Armenia Mainland
note: Clashes 12–14 September 2022 along Armenia border. ~204 Armenian soldiers killed or missing; 80 Azerbaijani. Azerbaijan occupied ~200 km² of Armenian sovereign land. Description says 'over 200 Armenian soldiers killed' which aligns. Facts accurate.

title: Lachin Corridor Blockade Forces Armenians From Karabakh
note: Blockade from December 2022; military operation 19–20 September 2023; near-total Armenian exodus (~100,000+) by end of September 2023. ICJ ordered free movement. HRW characterized as ethnic cleansing. All facts accurate.

title: COP29 Hosted in Baku — Oil State Leads Global Climate Talks
note: COP29 held Baku November 2024. Produced $300bn/year climate finance agreement (not described as such in event but event describes 'new climate finance agreement' which is accurate). All facts accurate.

title: Snap Presidential Election Extends Aliyev's Grip to 2031
note: Snap election 7 February 2024. Aliyev won 92.12%. Opposition boycotted. OSCE found neither free nor fair. Under 7-year term, extends to ~2031. All facts accurate.

title: Azerbaijan-Armenia Peace Treaty Negotiations Continue Without Resolution
note: Peace treaty negotiations ongoing into 2025 under EU and bilateral frameworks without final resolution. Consistent with publicly available reporting.

title: Southern Gas Corridor Expansion Advances as Europe Seeks Alternatives to Russia
note: SOCAR and EU engaged in SGC capacity expansion discussions throughout 2024–2025 following 2022 energy partnership. Consistent with publicly available reporting.
